# CLI Contract: Unified Dictate Startup
## Commands
```text dictate dictate serve dictate setup dictate setup --install-dependencies dictate doctor dictate devices ```
| Command | Contract | | --- | --- | | `dictate` | Starts the foreground combined Dictate invocation. It coordinates required local dependency services and enters normal dictation only after readiness succeeds. | | `dictate serve` | Compatibility alias with the same combined-invocation behavior and exit semantics as `dictate`. | | `dictate setup` | Read-only readiness/configuration probe; never acquires or launches dependencies. | | `dictate setup --install-dependencies` | The sole explicit path allowed to acquire/install local runtimes, models, and package dependencies. | | `dictate doctor` | Read-only, content-free diagnostic; never acquires or launches dependencies. | | `dictate devices` | Lists available input devices; never launches dependencies. |
## Combined Invocation Lifecycle
1. Validate configured dependency endpoints as local-only before making any content-bearing request or launching a dependency. 2. Acquire the single-invocation runtime lock. On contention, exit safely without managing dependency processes. 3. Probe the speech-recognition and cleanup dependencies. Mark each responding compatible local service as pre-existing. 4. Start only dependencies that are unavailable and record them as owned by this invocation. 5. Poll the complete readiness contract for no more than 30 seconds. 6. Start Dictate only after all required readiness checks succeed, then print the ready status and run until interrupted or a required owned dependency is lost. 7. On interruption, failed startup, timeout, or runtime dependency loss, stop Dictate and then stop only invocation-owned dependencies in reverse launch order. Release the runtime lock.
## Output and Exit Behavior
- Readiness is emitted exactly once per successful combined invocation, after Dictate and all required local capabilities are ready. - Startup, status, failure, and shutdown output uses fixed component/state/remediation language only. It MUST NOT contain audio, transcripts, context, prompts, generated text, or user-provided dictionary entries. - A missing runtime, model, executable, or verified artifact is a non-ready failure that directs the user to `dictate setup --install-dependencies`; it never triggers automatic acquisition. - Unsafe remote or non-loopback dependency endpoints are hard failures. The command MUST not launch, use, or fall back to a remote service. - Permission, device, hotkey, placement, launch, model, and timeout failures are non-ready failures. The command MUST not accept dictation after any such failure. - Lock contention fails with a fixed “Dictate is already running” message and no launch, attachment, reconfiguration, or shutdown of the other invocation. - Normal terminal interruption exits cleanly after owned-process cleanup. A failure exits non-zero; a normal user interruption may use the conventional interruption exit status.
## Ownership Rules
| Dependency state at invocation start | Startup action | Shutdown action | | --- | --- | --- | | Compatible local service is ready | Reuse it as pre-existing | Leave it running | | Service is unavailable | Launch the installed local service and await readiness | Stop it if this invocation launched it | | Endpoint is unsafe or incompatible | Fail before launch/use | Do not manage any external service | | Another invocation holds the lock | Fail safely | Do not manage any service |
## Compatibility and Boundaries
- The normal dictation workflow after ready—push-to-talk capture, local transcription, local cleanup, focus/target revalidation, and text insertion—retains its existing contract. - This contract adds no HTTP API, GUI, persistent daemon, remote access, cloud fallback, or user-content history.

# Data Model: Unified Dictate Startup
This feature introduces only transient operational state. It does not store audio, transcripts, context, prompts, generated text, or other user content.
## Combined Invocation
Represents one foreground `dictate` command execution.
| Field | Description | Validation | | --- | --- | --- | | invocation identifier | Opaque runtime identifier for lock ownership and diagnostics | Generated locally; never derived from user content | | state | `starting`, `waiting_ready`, `ready`, `recovering`, `stopping`, or `stopped` | State advances only through defined transitions | | deadline | Monotonic time by which readiness must succeed | Must be no more than 30 seconds after startup begins | | lock ownership | Whether this invocation holds the transient runtime lock | Required before starting managed dependencies | | application started | Whether `DictationService` successfully started | Must be false until all required readiness checks pass |
### State Transitions
```text starting -> waiting_ready -> ready -> stopping -> stopped starting -> stopping -> stopped waiting_ready -> recovering -> stopping -> stopped ready -> recovering -> stopping -> stopped ```
`recovering` is entered when an owned dependency exits or a required capability is lost after readiness. The invocation stops accepting dictation and emits only fixed content-free status before cleanup.
## Managed Dependency
Represents the local speech-recognition or cleanup dependency within one combined invocation.
| Field | Description | Validation | | --- | --- | --- | | name | Fixed dependency identifier: speech recognition or cleanup | Fixed non-content value | | endpoint | Configured local endpoint used for readiness and inference | Must pass existing loopback-only validation before launch or use | | initial state | `preexisting` or `unavailable` based on initial probe | Set before any launch attempt | | ownership | `preexisting` or `started_by_invocation` | Only `started_by_invocation` may be stopped by this invocation | | process state | `not_started`, `starting`, `ready`, `failed`, or `stopped` | Transitions are monotonic except `failed` to `stopped` during cleanup | | process handle | In-memory handle for a process launched by this invocation | Absent for pre-existing dependencies; cleared after stop |
### Rules
- A pre-existing dependency is never terminated, killed, reconfigured, or otherwise controlled by the combined invocation. - A dependency launch failure, readiness timeout, or unexpected owned-process exit transitions the invocation to safe cleanup. - A dependency endpoint that is non-local, authenticated, unsupported, or otherwise unsafe is rejected before launch and cannot become ready.
## Readiness Snapshot
A content-free result of the existing local checks.
| Field | Description | Validation | | --- | --- | --- | | speech recognition ready | Whether the local ASR health check passed | Required for ready | | cleanup ready | Whether the configured local model is ready | Required for ready | | microphone ready | Whether capture permission/device is available | Required for ready | | trigger ready | Whether global push-to-talk can be registered | Required for ready | | placement ready | Whether the platform can safely identify the insertion target | Required for ready | | limitations | Fixed non-content reasons for optional unavailable capabilities | Cannot include user content |
The combined invocation reports ready only when every required field is ready and `DictationService.start()` succeeds.
## Runtime Lock
A transient local coordination record used only while a combined invocation is active.
| Field | Description | Validation | | --- | --- | --- | | owner identifier | Opaque identifier of the current invocation | Compared atomically when releasing | | creation time | Operational timestamp | Used only to identify stale-lock recovery policy; contains no user content |
The lock is removed by the owning invocation in all normal, error, and interruption cleanup paths. Lock contention does not attach to, stop, or modify the existing invocation.

# Implementation Plan: Unified Dictate Startup
**Branch**: `002-unified-startup` | **Date**: 2026-08-12 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-unified-startup/spec.md`
## Summary
Make the installed `dictate` command the standard long-running entry point: safely coordinate locally installed Whisper and Ollama processes, wait for the complete Dictate readiness contract, and run the current dictation service. Add an invocation-scoped supervisor that probes dependencies before starting them, records ownership, polls existing content-free readiness checks under a bounded deadline, and stops only processes it launched. Keep `serve` as a compatibility alias and leave dependency acquisition exclusively in `setup --install-dependencies`.
## Technical Context
**Language/Version**: Python 3.11 or later
**Primary Dependencies**: Standard-library process, signal, URL, and time facilities; existing `sounddevice`, `pynput`, and platform-specific PyObjC packages; locally installed Whisper and Ollama executables
**Storage**: Existing local preferences and installer verification artifacts only; invocation ownership is in memory plus a transient local runtime lock with no user content
**Testing**: Python `unittest` discovery; existing unit, integration, and acceptance suites using fake loopback services and injected process handles
**Target Platform**: macOS, Windows, and Linux; platform readiness/placement support remains authoritative
**Project Type**: Local-first command-line application and long-running service
**Performance Goals**: In at least 95% of successful installed-system starts, report ready within 30 seconds; do not start DictationService until every required capability is ready
**Constraints**: Offline normal operation; loopback-only dependency endpoints; no automatic acquisition, cloud fallback, telemetry, persistence, or content in status output; cleanup must be bounded and idempotent; retain `serve` compatibility
**Scale/Scope**: One interactive local user and one active invocation per user runtime directory; no multi-user service, attachment/control protocol, GUI, or persistent daemon
## Constitution Check
*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*
**Pre-design gate: PASS**
- **Local-only operation**: The supervisor launches and verifies only local dependency endpoints. It does not invoke the installer or any network acquisition path, and all normal-path readiness and inference remain offline. - **Privacy by architecture**: Status, lock metadata, and logs contain fixed component/status information only. Audio, transcripts, prompts, context, and generated text remain in memory and are never used for supervision diagnostics. - **Lowest reasonable complexity**: A small supervisor and one Ollama process boundary reuse existing clients, `LocalReadiness`, `DictationService`, and standard-library process primitives. No new framework, database, daemon protocol, or platform process layer is introduced. - **CLI first and opinionated defaults**: No-argument `dictate` becomes the single default startup command; `serve` remains an alias. The existing explicit setup, diagnostic, and configuration commands remain separate. - **Cross-platform boundaries**: Process orchestration is platform-neutral; existing adapters continue to own permissions, hotkey, placement, and acquisition behavior. - **Fast/safe behavior and faithful transformation**: The existing dictation pipeline is unchanged and cannot run until safe readiness succeeds. - **Observable verification**: The implementation will add deterministic ownership, cleanup, lock-contention, offline, and content-free-output coverage.
**Post-design gate: PASS** — The proposed data model, CLI contract, and quickstart preserve all pre-design guarantees. The runtime lock is transient operational metadata, has no user content, and is removed on all exits; a locked invocation fails safely rather than attaching to or controlling another process.
## Project Structure
### Documentation (this feature)
```text specs/002-unified-startup/ ├── plan.md ├── research.md ├── data-model.md ├── quickstart.md ├── contracts/ │ └── cli.md └── tasks.md # Created by /speckit-tasks, not this phase ```
### Source Code (repository root)
```text src/dictate/ ├── bootstrap.py # Explicit-install-only bootstrap remains unchanged ├── cli.py # No-argument dispatch and compatibility alias ├── startup.py # New invocation-scoped dependency supervisor ├── asr.py # Whisper process boundary and client ├── cleanup.py # Ollama process boundary and client ├── readiness.py # Existing content-free capability probes ├── service.py # Existing DictationService lifecycle └── platform/ # Existing OS-only permissions/target/placement boundaries
tests/ ├── unit/ │ ├── test_cli.py │ ├── test_startup.py # New supervisor, ownership, timeout, and lock tests │ └── test_local_clients.py ├── integration/ │ └── test_unified_startup.py └── acceptance/ └── test_unified_startup.py ```
**Structure Decision**: Keep the existing single Python package and test layout. Add `startup.py` as the narrow composition root for lifecycle ownership rather than mixing dependency process control into CLI parsing, installer acquisition, platform adapters, or content-bearing inference clients.

# Quickstart: Validate Unified Dictate Startup
## Purpose
Validate that a fully installed Dictate environment starts the local speech-recognition service, local cleanup service, and Dictate application with one command, while preserving offline, privacy, and lifecycle guarantees.
See [CLI contract](contracts/cli.md) for command and ownership semantics and [data model](data-model.md) for transient lifecycle state.
## Prerequisites
- Use a supported operating system with Dictate installed as a terminal command. - Complete the explicit local dependency setup before this validation:
```bash dictate setup --install-dependencies ```
- Confirm the command reports local components/models installed. Do not manually start the local speech-recognition or cleanup services for the primary scenario. - For an offline check, disable network access after setup completes.
## Primary End-to-End Validation
1. Ensure the local speech-recognition and cleanup services are stopped. 2. Start Dictate:
```bash dictate ```
3. Expect one content-free ready status within 30 seconds. No additional terminal commands should be required to start either dependency. 4. Hold the configured push-to-talk trigger, speak a deterministic test phrase, and release it. 5. Verify text is inserted by the normal Dictate workflow. 6. Interrupt the foreground command using the terminal's normal interrupt key. 7. Verify the Dictate application and both dependency services launched by this command have stopped.
Expected result: startup, dictation, and shutdown complete without Internet access, cloud fallback, or content-bearing lifecycle output.
## Pre-existing Dependency Validation
1. Start one or both compatible local dependency services before launching Dictate. 2. Run:
```bash dictate ```
3. After ready status, interrupt Dictate. 4. Verify that each dependency that was already running remains available; verify that any dependency started by Dictate is stopped.
Expected result: dependency ownership is preserved exactly as defined in the [CLI contract](contracts/cli.md#ownership-rules).
## Failure and Safety Validation
Perform each scenario independently and capture only lifecycle output; use non-sensitive fixture data.
| Scenario | Action | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | Missing component/model | Make one required local component unavailable, then run `dictate` | Non-zero non-ready outcome with fixed remediation to `dictate setup --install-dependencies`; no acquisition occurs | | Unsafe endpoint | Configure a non-loopback dependency endpoint, then run `dictate` | Immediate non-ready failure before dependency launch or dictation | | Dependency never becomes ready | Cause a launched dependency to fail readiness | Non-ready timeout within 30 seconds; started dependencies are cleaned up | | Interrupted startup | Interrupt while readiness is pending | All dependencies started by the invocation stop before exit | | Permission failure | Deny microphone, trigger, or placement capability | Dictate never reports ready or accepts dictation | | Second invocation | Leave one `dictate` invocation active, then invoke `dictate` again | The second invocation fails safely without launching, attaching to, or stopping the first invocation's services | | Runtime dependency loss | Stop a dependency started by ready Dictate | Dictate enters content-free recovery, stops accepting new dictation, and cleans up owned services |
## Regression Checks
Run the project test suite after implementation:
```bash python -m unittest discover -s tests ```
Expected result: existing installer, offline, privacy lifecycle, pipeline, focus-safety, and platform matrix tests remain green, and unified-startup tests cover no-argument dispatch, ownership, cleanup, timeout, lock contention, and content-free output.

# Research: Unified Dictate Startup
## Decision: Use an invocation-scoped supervisor
Create a small `startup.py` coordinator that is called by no-argument `dictate` and the retained `serve` alias. It owns the sequence: validate local configuration, probe dependencies, launch only unavailable dependencies, wait for readiness, start `DictationService`, and clean up in `finally`.
**Rationale**: Current CLI logic performs readiness before starting the application, while Whisper process supervision is optional and unused by the CLI and Ollama has only a content-bearing HTTP client. A coordinator centralizes ownership, timeout, interruption, and lock semantics without entangling argument parsing, installer acquisition, or platform target operations.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Put all lifecycle logic in `cli.py`: rejected because it makes parsing, output, process ownership, polling, and cleanup difficult to test independently. - Extend `DictationService` to launch dependencies: rejected because the service should retain responsibility for hotkey/dictation lifecycle, not external process ownership. - Add a resident daemon with an attachment protocol: rejected as unnecessary complexity for one active local CLI invocation.
## Decision: Keep process boundaries separate from inference clients
Keep `WhisperServer` and `OllamaClient` focused on local inference/readiness requests. Provide a narrow managed process boundary for each executable; build Whisper's command from existing verified preferences and introduce the equivalent injected command/process boundary for Ollama.
**Rationale**: Separating launch/stop from content-bearing requests makes it explicit that only the supervisor decides ownership. It enables deterministic process tests and prevents a client connected to a pre-existing service from terminating it.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Make every client always launch its own service: rejected because it cannot preserve pre-existing services and obscures ownership. - Use platform installer adapters to launch processes: rejected because those interfaces are explicitly for acquisition and may perform network-enabled package operations.
## Decision: Probe first, then launch only unavailable local dependencies
Before launching each dependency, validate both configured endpoints with existing loopback URL validation and issue the existing content-free readiness probe. Mark a responding compatible service as pre-existing; otherwise attempt to start the corresponding local executable. Poll readiness until the shared deadline.
**Rationale**: This meets the one-command experience while retaining FR-010 ownership behavior. Existing URL validation rejects remote, authenticated, and non-HTTP endpoints before content-bearing processing can begin.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Always launch both executables: rejected because it produces port conflicts and risks disturbing manually managed services. - Treat a listening port as ready: rejected because model/application readiness is required in addition to a TCP listener.
## Decision: Use bounded polling and fixed, content-free startup status
Use an injected monotonic clock and sleeper to poll existing readiness checks until a 30-second deadline. Report only fixed component names, readiness state, and explicit remediation. Do not include exception strings that could contain configuration or user content.
**Rationale**: Readiness currently proves ASR, model, microphone, trigger, and placement capabilities but has no startup wait. Deterministic polling supports testability and prevents premature ready status.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Fixed sleep after process launch: rejected because startup time varies and can falsely report readiness. - Unbounded retries: rejected because it leaves users with a hung terminal and complicates cleanup.
## Decision: Fail safely on concurrent invocation via a transient local lock
Acquire a lock before launching or supervising dependencies. If another invocation owns it, print a fixed “already running” remediation and exit without launching or stopping any dependency. Remove the lock in `finally`, including failed startup and interruption paths.
**Rationale**: Safe failure satisfies the feature without needing an attachment/control protocol. It eliminates ownership ambiguity during another process's startup window.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Attach to the existing invocation: deferred; it needs a local control protocol and explicit process identity verification. - Infer ownership from endpoint availability: rejected because endpoint state cannot safely identify which invocation owns a process.
## Decision: Preserve explicit setup as the sole acquisition boundary
The default command and `serve` alias must never call `InstallerCoordinator`, package repair, model acquisition, or external runtime acquisition. Missing executable, model, or verified artifact produces a fixed failure directing the user to `dictate setup --install-dependencies`.
**Rationale**: The existing bootstrap and installer already enforce this boundary, which is required for offline normal operation and privacy.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Install missing dependencies while starting: rejected because it violates the explicit-user-action, offline-normal-operation contract.
## Decision: Stop only owned processes in reverse order
On normal interruption, startup failure, readiness timeout, application startup failure, or owned dependency loss: stop DictationService first, then stop only managed dependencies started by the invocation in reverse launch order. Process stop must be idempotent and bounded, using graceful termination followed by escalation if necessary.
**Rationale**: Reverse order removes dependents before their providers and preserves pre-existing services. Idempotence supports repeated cleanup through error and signal paths.
**Alternatives considered**:
- Let child processes outlive the CLI: rejected because it violates lifecycle ownership and leaves accidental background work. - Stop every reachable dependency: rejected because it may stop user-managed or another invocation's service.
